title_guess: Money market: participants and instruments (T-bill, CMB, CD, commercial bill, call money, repo, CP, money market mutual fund)
running_examples: T-bill: face value 1 lakh sold at a discounted price of 90K
commercial bill story: ABC sells goods to XYZ on 2-month credit, XYZ signs a bill of exchange, ABC discounts it at a bank, XYZ pays the bank on the due date (10.03.2023)
repo: a bank holding four securities needs cash and sells two to the RBI under a buy-back agreement
tenures: T-bill 14/91/182/364 days, CMB under 91 days, CD 7-364 days (AIFIs 1-3 years), CB 7-364 days, call money 1 day, notice money 2-14 days

best_moments.why: every participant gets the same pair of arrows: a security drops down into the green money-market ground and cash rises back up; borrowing = handing over paper for money, shown once and copied to all five

commercial bill told as a story with three flows: goods truck to XYZ on credit, bill of exchange curves back to ABC, bill goes down to the bank, cash rises to ABC, and XYZ's cash drops to the bank on the due date
repo: two of the bank's four securities glow, a 'sell' arrow lifts them to the RBI while cash drops, then a frame closes around both arrows as one deal and a contract sheet tagged REPO hooks on
T-bill chain: government emblem → security → RBI → banks & NBFCs, with face value 1 lakh against a 90K price tag: discount shown as two numbers on one certificate
the unorganised branch is ticked off with a scribbled 'done!' and set aside while the organised branch gets the RBI badge: scope of the lesson made visible

weak_moments.why: the participants strip sits for about 140 s with only three small callouts added; nothing shows what any participant does
certificate of deposit canvas is static for about 60 s while text callouts (AIFI list) carry the talk
call money is a definition paragraph plus a lend/borrow tick table; overnight inter-bank lending is never pictured
money market mutual fund is a paragraph and a bullet list only
the 14-day T-bill gets a red cross with no on-screen reason

segments.teaches: the financial market moves money from those with surplus funds to those short of funds; it splits into money market and capital market, and the money market into unorganised and organised (RBI-regulated)

elements.what: a hand passing a banknote over a small globe to an open hand; tags 'lend money / fund surplus' and 'borrow money / fund scarce', pointer 'money'
FINANCIAL MARKET
green bracket splits into money market | capital market with a wavy divider
money market splits into red unorganised and green organised
ticked checkbox and scribbled 'done!' on the pink unorganised box
RBI emblem beside a 'regulated by RBI' strip under organised

segments.notes: opening picture shrinks to the top at about 11 s to make room for the tree; same tree flashes back at the very end
segments.idea: money markets are one branch of financial markets, and the lesson covers only the organised, RBI-regulated part
segments.shown_as: a hand from a 'fund surplus' tag passes a banknote over a globe to a 'fund scarce' hand; the scene shrinks to the top and a green bracket splits FINANCIAL MARKET into money market and capital market; money market forks again into red unorganised and green organised; unorganised is boxed pink, ticked and scribbled 'done!' (set aside), organised gets a 'regulated by RBI' strip and the RBI emblem

segments.teaches: five kinds of players use the money market: RBI (for the government), banks (not regional rural banks), NBFCs, top-rated corporates, individuals; banks take demand and time deposits, NBFCs time deposits, corporates need a rating from an approved agency

MONEY MARKET with PARTICIPANTS underline
cream strip with five tick marks naming the participants, each with a small italic qualifier
speech-callouts over ticks: time deposit (NBFCs), demand & time deposit (banks), credit rating by approved agencies (corporates)

segments.notes: a list laid out on a ruler-like strip; the hands picture is decoration here; very slow (callouts at about 114, 143 and 185 s)
segments.idea: the money market's players are RBI, banks, NBFCs, top-rated companies and individuals, each with a condition
segments.shown_as: the lend/borrow hands return large above a MONEY MARKET heading; a cream strip with five tick marks writes the participants in one by one with italic qualifiers (for the government, except rural banks); much later small callouts pop over three ticks naming what each may take or need (time deposits, demand and time deposits, a credit rating)

segments.teaches: in the money market a borrower gives a short-term security and gets money; every participant can do both, and each deals with a set group (RBI only with banks and NBFCs; corporates and individuals with all except RBI)

segments.notes: this arrow pair (security down, cash up) becomes the video's visual grammar for every instrument after it
segments.idea: borrowing in the money market means handing a security into the market and taking cash out of it
segments.shown_as: the five participant names stand above a dark-green ground labelled MONEY MARKET; a hand holding banknotes rises out of the ground under NBFCs on yellow chevrons; then a security certificate drops on a down-arrow into the ground while a cash note rides an up-arrow out, and the same pair copies across to all five; bullets then write in under each, naming its counterparties

segments.teaches: the government issues treasury bills through the RBI to banks and NBFCs at a discount (pay 90K now for a bill worth 1 lakh at maturity)

segments.shown_as: the instrument list docks as a sidebar and the Treasury Bill chip lights up with a line into the canvas; the government emblem passes a security along an arrow to the RBI emblem; below RBI a security drops to 'banks & NBFCs' while a cash note rises back, a blue bar marks it 'government security at a discounted price', and a tag sets face value 1 lakh against price paid 90K

segments.shown_as: the issue chain collapses to an emblem-plus-certificate badge; a green elbow arrow drops to TREASURY BILL, which forks into four blue tenure chips; a red cross lands under 14 days; the sidebar highlight moves to Cash Management Bill and a second elbow arrow adds that name with a 'less than 91 days' bar

segments.teaches: banks raise short-term money by selling certificates of deposit to anyone in the money market: multiples of 1 lakh, minimum 1 lakh, 7-364 days; all-India financial institutions may issue CDs for 1-3 years

segments.notes: same issuer-arrow template as T-bill; last about 60 s static

segments.teaches: firm ABC sells goods to XYZ on two months' credit; XYZ gives ABC a bill of exchange, but ABC needs cash now

segments.teaches: call money is inter-bank borrowing for 1-14 days (call money 1 day, notice money 2-14 days); banks both lend and borrow, while AIFIs, insurers and mutual funds may only lend
